The e+e- -> pi+pi- total cross section contributes ~70% to the dispersive estimate of the leading-order hadronic term ahad,LO in the SM prediction of the muon anomalous magnetic moment.
The authors' estimate of ahad,LO(e+e-) = (696.2 ± 2.9) x 10^-10 is consistent with ahad,LO(e+e-) values obtained by other authors before the publication of the CMD-3 result.

The authors' SM prediction for the muon g-2, including their ahad,LO value, is aSM_tot = (11 659 184 ± 4) x 10^-10, which is 4.7 sigma smaller than the experimental value of aexp_tot = (11 659 205.9 ± 2.2) x 10^-10.
Excluding the CMD-3 pi+pi- data leads to a lower ahad,LO(e+e-) = (694.0 ± 2.0 ± 1.4 ± 0.4) x 10^-10, which translates to an SM prediction that is 5 sigma lower than the experimental value.

Considering only the CMD-3 pi+pi- data as the dominant experimental input for ahad,LO(pi+pi-) gives ahad,LO(e+e- -> pi+pi-,0.3-1.937 GeV) = (529.6 ± 2.8 ± 3.3 ± 3.3) x 10^-10, which corresponds to a total ahad,LO = (723.4 ± 3.1 ± 3.1 ± 3.5) x 10^-10 and an SM prediction consistent with the experimental value.

The authors confirm the observation made in the CMD-3 paper that the CMD-3 pi+pi- data, when taken alone, imply an SM prediction for the muon g-2 that is consistent with the experimental value at the ~1 sigma level.

The authors address the issue of incompatibility between the experimental measurements of the e+e- -> pi+pi- cross section by scaling the experimental uncertainties following the PDG prescription to achieve a consistent joint fit with chi^2/n_dof = 1.
The authors' total leading-order hadronic contribution to the muon g-2 is ahad,LO(e+e-) = (696.2 ± 1.9 ± 2.0 ± 0.8) x 10^-10.
The authors' ahad,LO value is consistent with the average value of ahad,LO(e+e-) = (693.1 ± 4.0) x 10^-10 obtained by the Muon g-2 Theory Initiative.
The authors use a model-independent parameterization of the e+e- -> pi+pi- cross section that should yield chi^2/n_dof ~ 1 when fitting to mutually compatible measurements.
The authors scale the experimental uncertainties by a common factor to account for missing systematic effects that cannot be identified within isolated experiments.
The authors apply the same uncertainty scaling procedure to all e+e- -> hadrons channels contributing to the dispersive estimate of ahad,LO.
The authors' analysis uses the program code developed for the PDG mini-review on sigma and R in e+e- collisions.
